stem.text: Evaluate the improper integral \( \int_{2}^{\infty} \frac{2 x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 5}}\,dx \), or show that it diverges.

worked_solution.text: The integral is improper because the upper limit of integration is infinite, so write it as \( \lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{2}^{R} \frac{2 x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 5}}\,dx \).
Substitute \( u = x^{2} + 5,\ du = 2 x\,dx \). The limits become \( u = 9 \text{ to } u = R^{2} + 5 \), and an antiderivative in u is \( 2 \sqrt{u} \).
Evaluate the limit: \( \lim_{R\to\infty} \left( 2\sqrt{R^{2} + 5} - 6 \right) = \infty \). The limit is infinite, so the integral diverges.

options.label: The integral converges to \( \infty - 6 \).
options.derivation: infinity substituted for the variable and the difference written as a value, with no limit

options.label: The integral converges to \( -6 \).
options.derivation: the p-integral formula for p > 1 applied with p = 1/2, which gives minus the antiderivative at the finite limit

options.label: The integral converges to \( -12 \).
options.derivation: the factor 1/2 from du dropped, then a finite value reported as in the first error
